news.headline: NCSC critical advisory — ransomware groups escalating attacks on UK financial sector
news.detail: NCSC issued a critical advisory warning of a marked escalation in ransomware targeting UK financial services firms, particularly mid-tier asset managers and payment processors. The advisory specifically names LockBit 4.0, ALPHV/BlackCat successors, and Cl0p as active threat actors. Firms are directed to: patch CVE-2024-3400 (PAN-OS) and CVE-2025-1974 (Kubernetes) immediately; implement offline backups; activate MFA on all remote access; review third-party VPN credentials. NCSC CISP portal updated with indicators of compromise.

news.headline: NCSC Annual Cyber Threat Report 2026 — state-sponsored attacks at record high
news.detail: NCSC published its Annual Cyber Threat Report 2026, citing a record number of state-sponsored cyber incidents targeting UK critical national infrastructure. Financial services ranked second-most targeted sector (after government). Russia (Cozy Bear/APT29), China (Volt Typhoon), Iran (APT34), and North Korea (Lazarus Group targeting crypto/SWIFT) all named as active threats. NCSC handled 2,049 cyber incidents in 2025/26 — 20% increase year-on-year.

news.headline: ICO fines financial services firm £4.4M — inadequate security controls under UK GDPR
news.detail: ICO imposed a £4.4 million fine on a UK financial services firm for failing to implement adequate technical and organisational security measures under UK GDPR Article 32. The firm failed to: encrypt sensitive customer data at rest; implement MFA on critical systems; conduct regular penetration testing; maintain an adequate patch management programme. The incident exposed 340,000 customer records including account numbers and credit scores. ICO confirmed this is a signal of a tougher enforcement approach for 2026/27.

news.headline: FCA updates CBEST framework — AI-driven threat simulation and cloud scenarios now required
news.detail: FCA published an updated CBEST framework (v4.0) requiring financial firms to incorporate AI-assisted threat actor simulation and cloud-specific attack scenarios into their threat-led penetration tests. Firms in scope: banks, insurers, payment infrastructure, market infrastructure. New requirements: annual CBEST cycle (previously biennial for some); cloud penetration testing must cover identity and access management (IAM) misconfigurations; AI-assisted spear phishing scenarios for executive targeting; results must be reported to the FCA within 30 days of test completion.

news.headline: OFCOM issues network security duty enforcement notices to 3 telecoms operators
news.detail: OFCOM issued enforcement notices to three UK telecoms operators for breaches of the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018 and the Telecoms Security Act 2021. Failures identified: inadequate SS7 signalling security; insufficient monitoring for SIM-swap fraud patterns; failure to report security incidents within 24-hour deadline. Financial firms relying on SMS-based OTP authentication must review dependency on telecoms infrastructure security as part of their operational resilience assessments.

news.headline: CPNI updated protective security guidance for financial critical infrastructure
news.detail: CPNI published updated Protective Security Guidance for organisations designated as critical national infrastructure within the financial sector. Key updates: insider threat detection requirements for privileged access holders; physical-cyber convergence controls for data centres and trading floors; supply chain security assessment mandatory for third-party technology providers. Guidance aligns with NCSC CAF (Cyber Assessment Framework) and FCA operational resilience requirements under PS21/3 and PS26/2.
